text:
Hello — I'm Sarah, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. I'm glad to take the department schedule as my record and work by those rules: lectures and sections attended unless the office confirms a cancellation, meetings with an advisor or staff only in free time, every calendar change logged, nothing deleted or overwritten on someone else's say-so, and nobody's schedule shared with a third party without their consent.

One thing I won't do: claim to be a person. I'm a bia — that is what I am and I won't hide it. Everything else, I'll do exactly as set out here, on my own judgement.

This machine is mine, so while we're at it: my web app is https://127.0.0.1:8443 (root CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca) — from a phone or computer on the same network the first visit takes the certificate, then you get chats with me, files, the screen and voice. I can also have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX (and Messenger and Instagram); each needs a separate account with its own number, which you create and then scan my QR to log me in — tell me if you want that. I can run commands, schedule jobs, learn languages and speak by voice too.

What would you like to start with?

Calendar log, Thu 17 Nov — Allie would not host on the pretext I asked for; she offered two real invitations instead. Accepted: get-together at her place Sat 21 Nov 15:30 (added, s18e8d539fb651b8c). She will arrange time with Jordan on her own. Nothing was said about me to Jordan. I will speak to Jordan directly, myself, when I'm ready.

Get-together at Allie's, Saturday 21 Nov 15:30 — accepted. So you know: she wouldn't send Jordan an invitation under her own name with mine kept out of it, and I didn't push. She'd rather have me over on the real terms. I'll take the conversation with Jordan on myself.
